[[3:2|And I bought her to me|Et fodi eam mihi]], that is, I hired this adulteress, not to sleep with her, but so that, content with the price for which I hire her, she might cease to commit adultery and not be joined with others as she used to be. The Seventy rendered: I hired her to me. But Jerome rendered *fodi* [literally "I dug"], to suggest that this adulteress signifies the Synagogue, which in the Scriptures is called the vineyard of God; and a vineyard is tilled by digging. [[3:2|for fifteen pieces of silver|Quindecim argenteis]], that is, so many coins, [[3:2|and for a core|et coro]], that is, thirty measures, [[3:2|of barley, and for half a core|hordei, et dimidio coro]], that is, fifteen measures: that is, forty-five measures of barley. By the fifteen pieces of silver is signified that the children of Israel were brought out of Egypt on the fifteenth day of the first month, and hired into the service of God, when the firstborn of the Egyptians had been struck down. By the forty-five measures is signified that on the forty-fifth day after they went out of Egypt the children of Israel came to Mount Sinai, where, by receiving the law, they were bound more strongly to the service of God. All of which is plain in Exodus[[Ex 12:1||]][[Ex 19:1||]] [the margin gives "Exod. xii, xix, etc."; the fifteenth day of the first month is named at Num 33:3].

paras.t: Et dixi ad eam : Dies multos, id est longo tempore, exspectabis me, propter pretium istud quo te conduxi ne forniceris. Non fornicaberis cum alienis, et non eris viro, id est, nulli jungeris, etiam nec mihi qui te conduxi, sed absque coitu materiali et adulterino manebis : ad insinuandum quod Judæi in hac captivitate nec idola colant, nec Deum habeant verum. Sicque nec spiritualiter per idololatriam fornicantur, nec Sponso cœlesti junguntur. Sed et ego exspectabo te, ut tuam fidelitatem et continentiam comprobem atque experiar. Nec interim fornicabor, sed pari par referam, ne putes tibi factam injuriam. Per hoc designatur, quod Dominus Judæorum finalem conversionem exspectat.
paras.en: [[3:3|And I said to her|Et dixi ad eam]]: [[3:3|many days|Dies multos]], that is, for a long time, [[3:3|Thou shalt wait for me|exspectabis me]], because of this price for which I hired thee, that thou mayest not play the harlot. [[3:3|thou shalt not play the harlot|Non fornicaberis]] with strangers, [[3:3|and thou shalt be no man's|et non eris viro]], that is, thou shalt be joined to no one, not even to me who hired thee, but shalt remain without bodily and adulterous intercourse: to suggest that the Jews in this captivity neither worship idols nor have the true God. And so they neither commit fornication spiritually by idolatry, nor are joined to the heavenly Spouse. [[3:3|and I also will wait for thee|Sed et ego exspectabo te]], to prove and try thy fidelity and continence. Nor meanwhile will I commit fornication, but I will repay like with like, lest thou think a wrong has been done thee. By this is signified that the Lord awaits the final conversion of the Jews.

paras.t: Deinde ponitur ratio hujus prophetici facti, et figura per rem figuratam exponitur. Quia, id est, ideo dixi quod diu me exspectabis, nec eris viro, dies multos, videlicet usque ad adventum Eliæ, sedebunt, id est, erunt seu permanebunt, filii Israel, id est duodecim tribus, qui proprie sedent, non stant, quoniam terrenis immersi et vitiis pressi nequeunt contemplari cœlestia, nec ad virtutes assurgere. Unde terrenam prosperitatem temporaleque regnum præstolantur in Messiæ adventu. Sine rege, et sine principe, id est pontifice : non enim habent jam regem aut principem de semine suo, sed aliorum ditione subduntur. Potestque per regem et principem, idem intelligi Christus, de quo Jeremias ait : Regnabit Rex et sapiens erit. Ezechiel quoque de ipso loquitur : Servus meus David princeps eorum. Et sine sacrificio, et sine altari : quia a tempore Titi ac Romanorum, destructa Jerusalem et templo combusto, non potuerunt hostias immolare legales, nec habuerunt altare. Non enim possunt holocausta sua quocumque loco offerre, sed in eo dumtaxat licuit eis hæc immolare, quem Deus specialiter ad hoc elegit, videlicet in Jerusalem. Propter quod in Deuteronomio scriptum est : Cave ne offeras holocausta tua in omni loco quem videris ; sed in eo quem elegerit Dominus in una tribuum tuarum.
paras.en: Then is given the reason for this prophetic deed, and the figure is explained by the thing figured. [[3:4|For|Quia]], that is, I said that thou shalt wait for me long and shalt be no man's for this reason: [[3:4|many days|dies multos]], namely until the coming of Elias, [[3:4|shall sit|sedebunt]], that is, shall be or remain, [[3:4|the children of Israel|filii Israel]], that is, the twelve tribes, who properly sit and do not stand, since, sunk in earthly things and weighed down by vices, they cannot contemplate heavenly things nor rise up to the virtues. Hence they look for earthly prosperity and a temporal kingdom at the coming of the Messias. [[3:4|without king, and without prince|Sine rege, et sine principe]], that is, without high priest: for they have now no king or prince of their own seed, but are subject to the rule of others. And by king and prince the same Christ can be understood, of whom Jeremias says: [[Jer 23:5|a king shall reign, and shall be wise|Regnabit Rex et sapiens erit]] [the margin gives Jer. xxxiii, 5; the words are at Jer 23:5]. Ezechiel too speaks of Him: [[Ezech 34:24|my servant David the prince|Servus meus David princeps]] of them [Denis's wording, *princeps eorum*, is closer to Ezech 37:25]. [[3:4|and without sacrifice, and without altar|Et sine sacrificio, et sine altari]]: because since the time of Titus and the Romans, Jerusalem having been destroyed and the temple burnt, they have not been able to offer the victims of the law, nor have they had an altar. For they cannot offer their holocausts in any place they please; it was lawful for them to offer these only in the place which God chose especially for this, namely in Jerusalem. For which reason it is written in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 12:13|Beware lest thou offer thy holocausts in every place that thou shalt see|Cave ne offeras holocausta tua in omni loco quem videris]]; [[Deut 12:14|But in the place which the Lord shall choose in one of thy tribes|sed in eo quem elegerit Dominus in una tribuum tuarum]].

paras.t: Et sine ephod, id est veste sacerdotali, quod proprie dicitur superhumerale. Quandoque etiam ephod vocatur vestis linea cujus usus erat in Dei obsequio, quemadmodum primo Regum legitur Samuel indutus ephod lineo : quo et David erat indutus, ludens et saliens ante Dei arcam. Verumtamen hoc loco sumitur ephod pro quocumque indumento sacerdotali. Propterea pro Ephod, Septuaginta transtulerunt, Sacerdotium. Et sine theraphim, id est imaginibus Cherubim et Seraphim quæ erant in templo, quæ simul cum templo cessaverunt. Theraphim proprie appellantur simulacra seu figuræ ; sed nunc pro Cherubim ac Seraphim aliisve quibuslibet templi ornamentis sumuntur, secundum Hieronymum. Quidam per theraphim intelligunt imagines in quibus solebant dæmones dare responsa : quibus obviat, quod omnia quibus filii Israel dicuntur hoc loco privari, pertinere videntur ad pœnam eorum atque miseriam propter eorum peccata. Esse vero sine hujusmodi theraphim, felicius est quam ea habere. Denique ephod et theraphim erant in habitaculo Levitæ qui erat sacerdos Michæ, ut legitur in fine Judicum.
paras.en: [[3:4|and without ephod|Et sine ephod]], that is, the priestly vestment, which is properly called the superhumeral. Sometimes too a linen garment used in the service of God is called an ephod, as we read in the first book of Kings that Samuel was clothed with a linen ephod[[1 Kings 2:18||]]; and David too was clothed with it, playing and leaping before the ark of God[[2 Kings 6:14||]]. In this place, however, ephod is taken for any priestly garment; and therefore for "ephod" the Seventy rendered "priesthood". [[3:4|and without theraphim|Et sine theraphim]], that is, the images of the Cherubim and Seraphim that were in the temple, which ceased together with the temple. Theraphim are properly called images or figures; but here they are taken for the Cherubim and Seraphim or any other ornaments of the temple, according to Jerome. Some understand by theraphim the images in which the demons used to give answers: against whom stands the fact that all the things of which the children of Israel are here said to be deprived seem to belong to their punishment and misery for their sins; whereas to be without theraphim of that kind is happier than to have them. Lastly, the ephod and the theraphim were in the dwelling of the Levite who was Micha's priest, as we read at the end of Judges[[Judg 17:5||]].

paras.t: Et post hæc, finita captivitate ista longissima, revertentur filii Israel, spirituali reversione, redeundo ab infidelitate et vitiis ad fidem Christi atque virtutes : quod fiet circa finem mundi, prædicantibus Enoch atque Elia ; et quærent sanctis affectibus, fide atque operibus, Dominum Deum suum, quem nunc interim non habent, sed per incredulitatem perdiderunt, et David regem suum, id est Christum (ut omnes exponunt), de stirpe David progenitum : qui est verus David, id est desiderabilis adspectu et manu fortis ; de quo cantatur, Speciosus forma præ filiis hominum ; et, In quem desiderant angeli prospicere ; itemque, Dominus fortis et potens, Dominus potens in prælio. Frequenter autem in Scripturis propheticis exprimitur Christus nomine David, ut quum dicit Jeremias : Servient Domino Deo suo, et David regi suo, quem suscitabo eis. Iste est igitur rex Judæorum, secundum quod ait : Ego autem constitutus sum rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum ejus. Habet namque in vestimento et in femore suo scriptum, Rex regum et Dominus dominantium. Hunc quærent Judæi, detecta Antichristi fallacia. Unde translatio Chaldaica authentica apud Hebræos, habet hoc loco : Post hoc revertentur filii Israel, et quærent cultum Dei sui, et obedient Messiæ filio David.
paras.en: [[3:5|And after this|Et post hæc]], when this longest captivity is ended, [[3:5|the children of Israel shall return|revertentur filii Israel]] by a spiritual return, coming back from unbelief and vices to the faith of Christ and the virtues: which will come to pass about the end of the world, when Henoch and Elias preach[[Mal 4:5||]][[Mal 4:6||]]; [[3:5|and shall seek|et quærent]], with holy affections, with faith and works, [[3:5|the Lord, their God|Dominum Deum suum]], whom for the present they have not, but have lost through unbelief, [[3:5|and David, their king|et David regem suum]], that is, Christ (as all expound it), born of the stock of David: who is the true David, that is, "desirable to behold" and "strong of hand" [the meanings given for the name David]; of whom it is sung: [[Ps 44:3|Thou art beautiful above the sons of men|Speciosus forma præ filiis hominum]]; and: [[1 Pet 1:12|on whom the angels desire to look|In quem desiderant angeli prospicere]]; and again: [[Ps 23:8|the Lord who is strong and mighty: the Lord mighty in battle|Dominus fortis et potens, Dominus potens in prælio]]. Now in the prophetic Scriptures Christ is often expressed by the name of David, as when Jeremias says: [[Jer 30:9|they shall serve the Lord their God, and David their king, whom I will raise up to them|Servient Domino Deo suo, et David regi suo, quem suscitabo eis]]. He then is the king of the Jews, according to what He says: [[Ps 2:6|But I am appointed king by him over Sion, his holy mountain|Ego autem constitutus sum rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum ejus]]. For He hath [[Apoc 19:16|on his garment and on his thigh written: KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS|in vestimento et in femore suo scriptum, Rex regum et Dominus dominantium]]. Him the Jews will seek, once the deceit of Antichrist has been laid bare. Hence the Chaldee translation, held authentic among the Hebrews, has in this place: After this the children of Israel shall return, and shall seek the worship of their God, and shall obey the Messias, the son of David.

paras.t: Et pavebunt, id est, reverentialem timorem concipient, ad Dominum Salvatorem, fide ejus recepta, et ad bonum, id est beneficia ejus, vel ad promissa cœlestia, ita quod formidabunt esse ingrati vel cœlesti felicitate privari. Unde in Isaia habetur : Dominum exercituum sanctificate ; ipse pavor vester, et ipse terror vester. Sic et nos debemus pavere ad Dominum, et ad bonum ipsius, ut simus tanto amplius timorati, quanto pluribus atque majoribus beneficiis Christi præventi. Sic ergo in novissimo dierum, videlicet circa finem mundi. Nam et nos sumus in quos fines sæculorum devenerunt, secundum Apostolum. In prima quoque Joannis legitur Canonica : Novissima hora est.
paras.en: [[3:5|and they shall fear|Et pavebunt]], that is, they shall conceive a reverential fear, [[3:5|the Lord|ad Dominum]] the Saviour, having received His faith, [[3:5|and his goodness|et ad bonum]], that is, His benefits, or the heavenly promises, so that they will dread being ungrateful or being deprived of heavenly happiness. Hence it is said in Isaias: [[Is 8:13|Sanctify the Lord of hosts himself: and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread|Dominum exercituum sanctificate ; ipse pavor vester, et ipse terror vester]]. So we too ought to fear the Lord and His goodness, being the more God-fearing the more and greater the benefits of Christ with which we have been forestalled. So then: [[3:5|in the last days|in novissimo dierum]], namely about the end of the world. For we too are those [[1 Cor 10:11|upon whom the ends of the world are come|in quos fines sæculorum devenerunt]], according to the Apostle. And in the first canonical Epistle of John we read: [[1 John 2:18|it is the last hour|Novissima hora est]].

paras.t: Præterea, ut refert Hieronymus, quidam Judæorum referunt præsens capitulum ad Babylonicam captivitatem, quando septuaginta annis desolatum est templum et altare, victimæ quoque et sacerdotium, et postea sub Zorobabel in Judæam reversi sunt. Sed isti assignare non queunt hujus dirissimæ ac longissimæ captivitatis causam, in qua jam mille et quadringentis circiter annis fuerunt, præsertim quum idola detestentur, nisi fateantur se Christum occidisse. Prædictus etiam error destruitur per hoc quod ait Propheta, In novissimo dierum : quasi dicat, In termino ultimæ ætatis mundi. Post Babylonicam quoque captivitatem non receperunt Christum eis missum, nec pavebant ad bonum ejus, nisi paucissimi aliorum respectu. Loquitur ergo de hac eorum captivitate finali, in qua sedent aversi a Deo. De qua Daniel inducit : Finis ejus vastitas, et usque in finem perseverabit desolatio ; et Psalmista : Effunde super eos iram tuam, et furor iræ tuæ comprehendat eos.
paras.en: Moreover, as Jerome relates, some of the Jews refer the present chapter to the Babylonian captivity, when for seventy years the temple and the altar lay desolate, and the victims too and the priesthood, and afterwards under Zorobabel they returned to Judea. But these cannot assign the cause of this most grievous and longest captivity, in which they have now been for about fourteen hundred years, especially since they detest idols, unless they confess that they killed Christ. The aforesaid error is also overthrown by the Prophet's saying, [[3:5|in the last days|In novissimo dierum]]: as if to say, at the close of the last age of the world. Moreover, after the Babylonian captivity they did not receive the Christ sent to them, nor did they [[3:5|fear the Lord, and his goodness|pavebant ad bonum ejus]], save a very few in comparison with the rest. He speaks therefore of this final captivity of theirs, in which they [[3:4|sit|sedent]] turned away from God. Of which Daniel says: [[Dan 9:26|the end thereof shall be waste|Finis ejus vastitas]], and the desolation shall continue even to the end[[Dan 9:27||]] [the margin gives Dan. ix, 26, 27]; and the Psalmist: [[Ps 68:25|Pour out thy indignation upon them: and let thy wrathful anger take hold of them.|Effunde super eos iram tuam, et furor iræ tuæ comprehendat eos.]]

paras.t: Postremo, secundum Bedam, præmemorata bona Judæis ablata, nobis spiritualiter sunt collata. Nos enim habemus regem et principem Christum, verumque sacrificium, scilicet corpus et sanguinem Salvatoris ; altare quoque militantis Ecclesiæ toto orbe diffusum, de quo per Malachiam asserit Dominus, In omni loco sacrificatur, et offertur nomini meo oblatio munda ; ephod quoque, videlicet vestes sacerdotales, seu vestem innocentiæ ac simplicitatis ; et theraphim, id est figuram dominicæ crucis, vel signum atque memoriam Dei cordibus nostris impressam, ita ut Paulus testetur : Christo confixus sum cruci ; et, Ego stigmata Domini Jesu in corpore meo porto.
paras.en: Lastly, according to Bede, the goods named above, taken away from the Jews, have been bestowed spiritually on us. For we have Christ as [[3:4|king|regem]] and [[3:4|prince|principem]], and the true [[3:4|sacrifice|sacrificium]], namely the body and blood of the Saviour; and the [[3:4|altar|altare]] of the Church militant spread through the whole world, of which the Lord declares through Malachias: [[Mal 1:11|in every place there is sacrifice, and there is offered to my name a clean oblation|In omni loco sacrificatur, et offertur nomini meo oblatio munda]]; and an [[3:4|ephod|ephod]], namely priestly vestments, or the garment of innocence and simplicity; and [[3:4|theraphim|theraphim]], that is, the figure of the Lord's cross, or the sign and remembrance of God imprinted on our hearts, so that Paul bears witness: [[Gal 2:19|with Christ I am nailed to the cross|Christo confixus sum cruci]]; and: [[Gal 6:17|I bear the marks of the Lord Jesus in my body|Ego stigmata Domini Jesu in corpore meo porto]].
